flashcard_questions.q: What is a Local Area Network?
flashcard_questions.a: A network covering a small area on one site, such as a school or office.

flashcard_questions.q: What is a Wide Area Network?
flashcard_questions.a: A network covering a large area that joins LANs together, often over leased infrastructure.

flashcard_questions.q: Which is the largest wide area network in the world?
What is bandwidth on a network connection?
flashcard_questions.a: The maximum amount of data a connection can carry in a given time.

flashcard_questions.q: Which network device uses MAC addresses to send data to one device on a LAN?
Which network device joins different networks together using IP addresses?
What does the Domain Name System do when you type a web address?
flashcard_questions.a: It looks up the IP address of the server that hosts the website.

flashcard_questions.q: How many bits long is an IPv4 address?

flashcard_questions.a: A permanent number built into a device network card by its manufacturer.

flashcard_questions.q: Which topology gives every device its own cable to a central switch?
Why does a mesh topology have no single point of failure?
flashcard_questions.a: If one link breaks the data simply takes another route.

flashcard_questions.q: Which protocol transfers web pages between a web server and a browser?
Which protocol is the encrypted version used for logins and payments?
Which protocol sends emails and passes them between mail servers?
Why are network protocols organised into layers?
flashcard_questions.a: Each layer handles one part, so it can be changed without breaking the others.

notes: 15 cards: 5 term-to-definition, 3 device-to-role, 3 protocol-to-purpose, 2 topology, 1 number fact, 1 causal. This lesson is very broad, so peer-to-peer, cloud, FTP, POP, IMAP and IPv6 were left out to keep the deck at 15 and avoid protocol interference.
